goal: Check code and its changes for audit and compliance evidence: logging, change records, access control and ret…
use: Check code and its changes for audit and compliance evidence: logging, change records, access control and retention. Use when preparing for an audit or when a change touches regulated data.

steps.note: Read the scope. Identify the regulated data or controls this code touches, and the policy it must meet.
Check audit logging. Security-relevant events (sign-in, permission change, data export, deletion) must be logged with who, what, when and the result.
Check log safety. Flag secrets, passwords, tokens and personal data written to logs.
Check change records. Each change should have a linked ticket, a reviewer and a passing check.
Check access control. Flag shared accounts, hard-coded credentials and admin actions without a second check.
Check retention. Flag data kept with no deletion path, and deletion that does not reach backups or copies where the policy requires it.

protocol.title: Read the scope
protocol.text: Identify the regulated data or controls this code touches, and the policy it must meet. If no policy is given, ask for it rather than assume one.

protocol.title: Check audit logging
protocol.text: Security-relevant events (sign-in, permission change, data export, deletion) must be logged with who, what, when and the result. Flag events with no log.

protocol.title: Check log safety
protocol.text: Flag secrets, passwords, tokens and personal data written to logs.

protocol.title: Check change records
protocol.text: Each change should have a linked ticket, a reviewer and a passing check. Flag merges with no review.

protocol.title: Check access control
protocol.text: Flag shared accounts, hard-coded credentials and admin actions without a second check.

protocol.title: Check retention
protocol.text: Flag data kept with no deletion path, and deletion that does not reach backups or copies where the policy requires it.

protocol.title: Report
protocol.text: For each control give the status: evidence present, partly present, or missing. Say what must be collected from outside the repository. This is a technical aid, not a certification. Mark what you did not run.
